summary: BBN's traffic statistics for the ARPANET hosts for March 1973, as tables of packets output per host. Data for two days was missing. It updates RFC 482 and was itself updated by RFC 509.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC publishes host traffic statistics for March 1973. Its tables show packet output by host and separate traffic between nodes from traffic within a node.

subtitle: A BBN table of ARPANET host packet output for March 1973.

tldr.problem: Network operators wanted a record of how much packet traffic each host generated.
tldr.mechanism: The report lists packet output per host, separating internode and intranode counts and including totals and averages.
tldr.outcome: This is a monthly data report, not a protocol. It updates RFC 482 and was updated by RFC 509.

sections.title: The March Traffic Report
sections.content:
A. McKenzie of BBN-NET provides host traffic statistics for March 1973. The report consists of a Host Throughput Summary of packets output and notes that data is missing for March 16 and 20.

The document reports network measurements rather than defining a protocol or procedure.
sections.plainLanguage: This is a monthly report of packets sent by ARPANET hosts. It notes that data for two days is missing.

sections.title: Per-Host and Site Figures
sections.content:
The table lists hosts by site and host number. It separates packets sent between nodes (internode) from packets sent within a node (intranode), and gives a total for each host. Sites with several hosts also have grouped totals and daily internode averages.

The report identifies BELV and LBL as having no traffic. Its site entries show the number of days represented in the reported average.
sections.plainLanguage: Each host has counts for traffic to other nodes and traffic within its own node. The table also provides totals and averages for sites.

sections.title: Network-Wide Summary
sections.content:
The final lines report network-wide totals of 56405660 internode packets and 20045130 intranode packets. They also give daily averages of 1945023 internode packets and 691212 intranode packets.

The report gives an average of 54028 internode and 19200 intranode packets per node-day. It also lists an internode packets-to-messages ratio of 1.08.
sections.plainLanguage: The bottom of the report gives overall packet totals and daily averages. It also reports the average number of packets per message for internode traffic.

references.text: RFC 482, updated by this March 1973 traffic report.
